changedBeliefs: The selectBytes encoder's structural framing — the per-row `{` / `}` and inter-row `,` writes in `write_json_to_buf` — is below the noise floor. Batching the inter-row `}` + `,` + `{` into a single `buf_write("},{", 3)` (with the final `}` emitted once after the loop, output byte-identical) moved `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` by −0.3% to −3.9% on the 10k-row shapes, but the deltas did not reproduce across the order flip (the −3.9% on 10k×20 int collapsed to −0.4%; the mixed shape flipped sign to +1.8%) and the control moved as much as the targets — all inside the ~2.5% baseline-to-baseline noise.

After exp 190/192/194/195 tightened the per-cell token and value work, encoder wall is dominated by the per-cell formatters (`fast_i64_to_str`, `fast_double_to_json_num`) and `json_write_string`'s SWAR escape scan, which run once per cell — not by the once-per-row `buf_write` framing calls.
nextSignals: Do not retry batching the structural JSON framing (`{`, `}`, `,`) in `write_json_to_buf` without profiler evidence that `buf_write` / `buf_write_char` call overhead is a material share of selectBytes wall on a specific shape — `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` shows it is not at 10k × 2–20 columns.
Remaining selectBytes encoder headroom, if any, is in the per-cell value formatters or the transfer path, not the row framing. Treat structural framing as settled.
